response_change.parent_relation: Consumer growth from feeding is linear in resource abundance at fixed consumer abundance: dC_dt/C = conversion_efficiency * encounter_rate * R - consumer_mortality_rate.
response_change.child_relation: Consumer growth from feeding rises with resource abundance at low R but approaches a finite per-capita maximum at high R because handling/processing limits consumer recruitment.
response_change.observable_effect: When C is held fixed and R varies over low-to-high values along observed trajectories, the parent predicts an unbounded linear increase in per-capita consumer growth with R, whereas the child predicts diminishing returns and a bounded maximum growth rate.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when resource abundance becomes large enough that encounter-limited feeding is no longer the sole bottleneck, i.e. along trajectories with moderate-to-high R relative to the consumer's implicit processing scale; at low R the child should reduce approximately to the parent.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, low and moderate R can look nearly linear; in holdout with higher realized R from the same initial-condition protocol, the child shows compressed peaks in dC_dt/C versus R instead of the parent's continued linear increase.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of negligible handling limitation (saturation scale taken very large, or equivalently over trajectories restricted to low R), the child law converges to the parent mass-action recruitment term.
plan.gap_statement: The current consumer recruitment term assumes every additional resource individual increases consumer birth rate proportionally without bound, omitting processing/handling saturation in consumer reproduction from feeding.
plan.baseline_assumption: Encounter and conversion conditions are constant over time and effectively unlimited, so conversion_efficiency * encounter_rate acts as a single linear gain on R in the consumer equation.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite handling or assimilation capacity per consumer causes a Holling type II style saturation of feeding-derived consumer recruitment.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the linear mass-action assumption for feeding-derived consumer recruitment while keeping the same states. The parent target mapping has a single_gain shortcut: at fixed C, the scored quantity dC_dt depends on R through one shared linear coefficient, so its slope with respect to R is constant. Scientifically, this is idealized because consumers cannot convert prey into offspring arbitrarily fast once capture, digestion, or egg production becomes rate-limiting. The child therefore changes the response from linear to saturating, producing an asymptotic change in the mapping from observed states to dC_dt itself, not merely in auxiliary trajectories. Distinguishing condition: vary realized resource abundance R along the jointly evolved trajectories while holding the parameter set fixed and comparing per-capita consumer growth dC_dt/C across low versus high R. Under admissible nonnegative states, the parent predicts the same marginal increase in dC_dt/C for each added unit of R, but the child predicts a smaller marginal increase at high R and a bounded maximum feeding contribution. This contrast is observable only when trajectories visit sufficiently large R; if all observed R remain small, the refinement is weak and effectively collapses back toward the parent. No new state is needed because the omitted mechanism is a different functional form for an already present feeding process rather than a separate latent stock.

contract.assumption_before: Feeding-derived consumer recruitment is encounter-limited and proportional to resource abundance across the entire observed range.
contract.assumption_after: Feeding-derived consumer recruitment is encounter-limited only at low resource abundance and becomes handling/processing-limited at higher resource abundance.
contract.before_fragment: conversion_efficiency * encounter_rate * R * C - consumer_mortality_rate * C
contract.after_fragment: conversion_efficiency * encounter_rate * R * C / (1 + handling_saturation_scale * R) - consumer_mortality_rate * C
contract.parent_reduction: As handling_saturation_scale -> 0, or when handling_saturation_scale * R << 1 over the observed trajectories, the child expression approaches the parent expression.
contract.observable_signature: At fixed C, plotting dC_dt/C against R gives a straight line in the parent but a concave, saturating curve in the child, with the divergence becoming visible once handling_saturation_scale * R is not small.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set can change only the overall slope conversion_efficiency * encounter_rate and offset consumer_mortality_rate, so it still predicts d(dC_dt/C)/dR = conversion_efficiency * encounter_rate everywhere. The child instead predicts a decreasing slope and bounded feeding contribution at high R, which no fixed parent coefficient set can match simultaneously across both low-R and high-R conditions visited under the same trajectory protocol.

range_suggestions.handling_saturation_scale: positive; small values approach mass-action behavior, larger values activate saturation over the observed resource range

response_change.parent_relation: Feeding-derived consumer recruitment increases with resource abundance R through a single Holling type II saturation term, so at fixed C the per-capita consumer growth contribution is a monotone concave function of R with one shared saturation scale.
response_change.child_relation: Keep encounter-driven recruitment but relax the assumption that handling limitation acts only through resource abundance; introduce consumer-density interference in the same feeding term so that, at fixed R, rising C depresses per-capita recruitment and, at fixed C, the dependence on R saturates differently across consumer crowding levels.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories that reach similar R but different C, the child predicts lower dC_dt at higher C because crowding reduces effective feeding/recruitment; the parent can only scale linearly with C outside mortality and cannot reproduce this C-dependent bending of the recruitment term with one shared parameter set.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when consumer abundance is large enough that consumer-consumer interference during foraging is not negligible over the same range of R where handling saturation already matters; practically, moderate to high C with positive R and especially periods after consumer peaks in the joint dynamics.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as weaker-than-linear growth of feeding-derived gains with C during crowded phases; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to stronger suppression of recruitment near larger consumer peaks without changing the low-C limit.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing consumer interference strength, or whenever C stays low enough that interference is negligible compared with the baseline handling term.
plan.gap_statement: The current consumer equation assumes each consumer's feeding-derived recruitment is limited only by resource handling saturation, omitting reduction of feeding success caused by consumer crowding or interference.
plan.baseline_assumption: Encounter and conversion conditions are constant over time and individuals are equivalent, with no explicit consumer-density effect on per-consumer feeding beyond the multiplicative C factor.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Mutual interference among consumers during search, attack, or kleptoparasitic disruption reduces realized feeding/recruitment at high consumer density, yielding a Beddington-DeAngelis/Crowley-Martin-type refinement of the functional response.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-threshold assumption that only resource abundance controls saturation of feeding-derived consumer growth. In the parent, holding R fixed gives dC_dt = C*(const(R)-consumer_mortality_rate), so the feeding contribution is exactly linear in C and all curvature with respect to abundance enters only through R. Varying consumer crowding along the observed joint trajectories therefore cannot change the per-capita feeding gain except through indirect changes in R. A child with consumer interference changes the target mapping itself: at the same observed R but larger C, per-capita recruitment falls because foragers impede one another. This is directly observable under the existing initial conditions because predator-prey cycles naturally generate phases with positive R and differing C, especially around and after consumer peaks. The contrast is not merely in auxiliary trajectories; it changes dC_dt as a function of the supplied states (R,C). A single refit of the parent cannot reproduce both low-C near-linear scaling and high-C suppressed feeding across these conditions, because its only C dependence is the external factor C minus linear mortality, whereas the child adds C inside the feeding nonlinearity. The refinement remains scientifically admissible, preserves nonnegativity, and smoothly reduces to the parent when interference is negligible.

contract.before_fragment: conversion_efficiency * encounter_rate * R * C / (1 + handling_saturation_scale * R) - consumer_mortality_rate * C
contract.after_fragment: conversion_efficiency * encounter_rate * R * C / (1 + handling_saturation_scale * R + consumer_interference_scale * C) - consumer_mortality_rate * C
contract.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when consumer_interference_scale -> 0, or approximately whenever consumer_interference_scale * C is negligible relative to 1 + handling_saturation_scale * R.
contract.observable_signature: Holding R fixed and positive, the parent gives a feeding contribution exactly proportional to C, whereas the child gives sublinear growth in C because C also enlarges the denominator. Holding C fixed, the child still saturates in R, but the effective recruitment level is lower under higher consumer crowding, so two trajectory segments with similar R and different C can show different dC_dt values beyond the parent's linear mortality offset.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of all parent parameters cannot match both the low-C near-parent regime and the high-C interference-suppressed regime across the same observed R range, because in the parent the feeding term is C multiplied by a function of R only. Retuning encounter_rate, conversion_efficiency, handling_saturation_scale, or consumer_mortality_rate changes gain or the single R-threshold globally, but it cannot create the child’s extra C dependence inside the recruitment nonlinearity.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed consumer abundance C, feeding-derived consumer growth increases with resource abundance R as a single saturating Beddington-DeAngelis curve with one shared saturation scale, so the recruitment-vs-R curvature does not change qualitatively with recent resource history.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the assumption of instantaneous conversion of consumed resource into new consumers with a delayed maturation pipeline represented by a juvenile consumer state. Then dC_dt depends on recruitment from the juvenile pool rather than directly on current feeding, so the instantaneous adult growth response to current R becomes history-dependent and can lag behind current feeding conditions.
response_change.observable_effect: After a resource pulse or during fast predator-prey oscillations, the parent predicts immediate adult-growth acceleration when R rises, whereas the child predicts strong current feeding with only delayed adult increase; thus two times with similar current (R,C) but different recent trajectories can show different dC_dt.

plan.activation_condition: Most visible when resource abundance changes on timescales comparable to consumer maturation, such as during repeated predator-prey cycles or transient resource pulses; weak when maturation is effectively instantaneous relative to population change.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training regions with moderate oscillations, the lag appears as softened and delayed adult-growth peaks relative to feeding flux; in holdout with sharper or larger-amplitude resource swings, the same maturation mechanism produces stronger phase lag and altered peak timing rather than merely a rescaled gain.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the fast-maturation limit where juvenile residence time tends to zero and juvenile mortality is negligible, so feeding-derived production is converted almost instantaneously into adult consumer growth.
plan.promotion_reason: A genuine maturation delay is not representable with only the current adult consumer and resource states, because dC_dt must depend on stored past feeding through an internal population compartment rather than a memoryless function of current R and C.
plan.gap_statement: The model treats all feeding-derived recruitment as instantly appearing in the reproducing/mortality-bearing consumer class, omitting juvenile development time.
plan.baseline_assumption: Individuals within each population are equivalent, so there is no stage structure and no delay between resource consumption and addition to the consumer population counted by C.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Consumed resources first generate immature consumers that survive and mature into adults after a finite developmental period.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the instantaneous-conversion assumption by introducing juvenile consumers. In the parent, holding C fixed, increasing R immediately raises dC_dt through the same saturating feeding term, so the adult response is a single-phase memoryless function of current states. In the child, current feeding still creates consumers, but they enter a juvenile compartment first; adult dC_dt is then governed by maturation inflow minus adult mortality. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only an auxiliary trajectory, because the target is dC_dt and it no longer follows current feeding instantaneously. The contrast is observable under the actual ODE protocol from the given initial conditions once trajectories generate varying recent histories: for similar current R and C reached on the rising versus falling side of a cycle, the child can produce different dC_dt due to different juvenile backlog, while a single parent parameter set cannot because its dC_dt is uniquely determined by current R and C. The effect is scientifically admissible when developmental delay is not negligible relative to ecological turnover; if maturation is extremely fast, the refinement collapses back to the parent.

The parent gives the same dC_dt because its target mapping is uniquely determined by current (R,C), while the child can give different dC_dt because J retains recent feeding history; the contrast is strongest when feeding_flux changes on the same scale as 1/juvenile_maturation_rate.

response_change.parent_relation: The adult consumer growth term is linear in juvenile abundance alone, dC_dt = juvenile_maturation_rate * J - consumer_mortality_rate * C, so at fixed C the slope of dC_dt with respect to J is constant and independent of resource conditions.
response_change.child_relation: Replace constant per-capita juvenile maturation with resource-dependent maturation, so the contribution of J to dC_dt depends jointly on J and R; at fixed C and J, adult gain is reduced under resource scarcity and approaches the parent form when resources are abundant.
response_change.observable_effect: Across times or trajectories with similar juvenile abundance J but different resource abundance R, the same juvenile pool yields different adult recruitment rates; low-R periods show weaker conversion of J into C than high-R periods.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when resource abundance varies over time enough that juveniles experience both low-resource and moderate/high-resource conditions before maturing; strongest when juvenile maturation is not effectively instantaneous and R can transiently become small relative to its typical initial scale.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, ordinary predator-prey cycling already creates windows with similar J but differing R. In holdout trajectories with deeper resource troughs or longer juvenile residence times, the contrast strengthens because resource-poor periods suppress maturation more strongly than the parent allows.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where maturation is resource-insensitive, equivalently when the resource-limitation effect on maturation vanishes or when R stays uniformly high over the observed interval.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes juvenile consumers mature into adults at a constant per-capita rate regardless of present resource conditions, even though juveniles often require continued feeding or favorable energetic conditions to complete development.
plan.baseline_assumption: The parent fixes juvenile_maturation_rate as constant in time and independent of system state.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Resource-dependent juvenile development: maturation slows under resource scarcity because juveniles lack sufficient food or condition to complete development, and approaches the baseline rate when resources are plentiful.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the constant-maturation assumption rather than adding an unrelated new compartment. The parent target mapping has a single_gain shortcut: once J and C are known, R cannot modify dC_dt except indirectly through past effects on J. Scientifically, that omits a common developmental bottleneck in which juveniles produced earlier may remain unable to mature during current resource shortage. Vary resource abundance R while holding J and C fixed conceptually at matched observed values. Parent prediction gives the same adult gain for both cases because the slope with respect to J is fixed at juvenile_maturation_rate. The child predicts lower adult gain at low R and near-parent gain at high R, creating a direct R-by-J interaction in the scored target mapping. This contrast is admissible under the existing observation protocol because R, J, and C are all supplied states and the system’s own cycles can generate matched J with differing R. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce this state-dependent slope change across such conditions: changing juvenile_maturation_rate rescales all J equally, whereas the child changes the effective slope only in low-resource regimes. The limitation is that if R never varies appreciably or stays always high, the refinement becomes weakly identifiable and the parent is recovered approximately.

response_change.child_relation: Replace constant per-capita juvenile maturation with resource-dependent maturation, so the contribution of J to dC_dt depends jointly on J and R; at fixed C and J, adult gain is reduced under resource scarcity and approaches the parent form when resources are abundant.
response_change.observable_effect: Across times or trajectories with similar juvenile abundance J but different resource abundance R, the same juvenile pool yields different adult recruitment rates; low-R periods show weaker conversion of J into C than high-R periods.

response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that the same saturating factor fully captures juvenile maturation quality; allow maturation success to become unimodal in resource abundance because extreme resource abundance can reduce juvenile-to-adult transition efficiency through crowding, poor condition, or toxic/algal-bloom-like low-quality food. Then at fixed J, dC_dt rises with R at low-intermediate resource levels but bends over more strongly, potentially peaking and declining at very high R.

plan.scientific_mechanism: Overabundant resource can become low-quality or physiologically stressful for juveniles, making maturation success unimodal rather than purely saturating.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the maturation assumption, not add an unrelated new compartment. The parent target mapping is dC_dt(R,C,J)=J*juvenile_maturation_rate*R/(1+handling_saturation_scale*R)-consumer_mortality_rate*C, so when C and J are held fixed its dependence on R is constrained to one monotone saturating shape. Varying resource abundance along observed trajectories while comparing times with similar juvenile abundance gives a concrete test: under the parent, increasing R can only increase the maturation contribution toward a plateau; under the child, sufficiently high R can reduce realized adult recruitment relative to intermediate R. This is a changed target mapping, not merely a different auxiliary trajectory, because R enters the scored equation directly. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both intermediate-resource enhancement and high-resource suppression across admissible conditions, since its derivative with respect to R remains nonnegative for all R>=0. The mechanism is scientifically admissible in systems where bloom-like or overcrowded resource conditions reduce nutritional quality or developmental success. Limitation: if the sampled trajectories never reach high R, the refinement will be weakly identifiable and should honestly collapse back toward the parent.

response_change.parent_relation: Adult consumer growth from juveniles is proportional to J times a single resource-dependent maturation factor R/(1 + handling_saturation_scale*R), so at fixed J the dependence of dC_dt on resource abundance has one fixed saturating curvature and no high-resource decline.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that the same saturating factor fully captures juvenile maturation quality; allow maturation success to become unimodal in resource abundance because extreme resource abundance can reduce juvenile-to-adult transition efficiency through crowding, poor condition, or toxic/algal-bloom-like low-quality food. Then at fixed J, dC_dt rises with R at low-intermediate resource levels but bends over more strongly, potentially peaking and declining at very high R.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar J but different high-resource levels, the parent predicts adult production should keep increasing toward a plateau, whereas the child predicts reduced adult production at sufficiently high R after an intermediate optimum.

contract.activation_condition: The refinement is observable only when trajectories enter a very high-resource regime relative to the maturation scale, with nonzero juvenile abundance so maturation contributes materially to dC_dt; at low to moderate R the child should reduce to the parent-like monotone increase.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as stronger-than-parent flattening of adult recruitment at upper-range resource abundance; in holdout with still higher R it extends to a clear turnover or sharper suppression that the parent's single saturating gain cannot match with one parameter set.
contract.continuation_path: In the limit of negligible high-resource inhibition or outside the high-R regime, the maturation law returns to the parent's monotone saturating form.
contract.domain_mechanism: Competing facilitation and inhibition of juvenile maturation across the resource gradient
contract.scientific_mechanism: Overabundant resource can become low-quality or physiologically stressful for juveniles, making maturation success unimodal rather than purely saturating.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because it makes the scored target law the product of a facilitating maturation term and a competing inhibitory process, changing the curvature of dC_dt as a function of observed resource abundance and allowing turnover at high R.
contract.assumption_before: Resource-dependent juvenile development is represented by a single monotone Holling-type saturation with no adverse high-resource effect.
contract.assumption_after: Juvenile maturation combines the original saturating resource benefit with a competing high-resource inhibition that reduces successful maturation at extreme resource abundance.
contract.before_fragment: juvenile_maturation_rate * R / (1 + handling_saturation_scale * R) * J - consumer_mortality_rate * C
contract.after_fragment: juvenile_maturation_rate * R / (1 + handling_saturation_scale * R) * exp(-high_resource_inhibition_scale * R) * J - consumer_mortality_rate * C
contract.parent_reduction: Setting high_resource_inhibition_scale = 0 recovers the parent exactly.
contract.observable_signature: When trajectories reach very high resource abundance relative to the maturation scale and J remains nonzero, the parent target mapping from observed states predicts maturation contribution to dC_dt should continue increasing toward a plateau, while the child mapping predicts stronger bending and possible decline of that contribution at extreme R. This changed target mapping is directly observable in the scored C equation, not only through auxiliary state trajectories.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both intermediate-resource enhancement and high-resource suppression across these admissible conditions because the parent maturation contribution juvenile_maturation_rate*R*J/(1 + handling_saturation_scale*R) is monotone nondecreasing in R for J > 0. Retuning gain or saturation scale can shift the plateau level and approach rate but cannot create a decline in the scored mapping from observed R, J, and C to dC_dt.

range_suggestions.high_resource_inhibition_scale: 0 <= high_resource_inhibition_scale <= 1/initial_resource_scale; zero recovers the parent, positive values activate high-resource maturation suppression
